features.text: The patient has been experiencing fluctuating blood pressure, with readings up to 180 mmHg.
The patient has experienced lightheadedness and slight headaches associated with the elevated blood pressure.
The patient has had a slight heaviness in the chest, but it is not prolonged.
The patient has no trouble breathing.
The patient has a history of essential hypertension.
The patient is currently taking lisinopril 20 milligrams twice per day for hypertension.
The patient has hyperlipidemia and is taking atorvastatin for cholesterol management.
The patient has osteoarthritis and uses tylenol for pain when needed.
The patient has no family history of hypertension or cardiovascular disease.
The patient has not experienced syncope or palpitations during the episodes of elevated blood pressure.
The patient has not experienced vision changes, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking during the episodes of high blood pressure.
The patient has a grade three out of six systolic ejection murmur.
The patient has mild bibasilar rales in the lungs.
The patient has trace lower extremity edema.
The patient has not had an echocardiogram recently and is willing to undergo one if needed.
The patient has not had recent blood tests, including renal function tests, electrolytes, or an ECG.
The patient has pending renal function tests (serum creatinine, estimated GFR), electrolytes, and ECG results, which are expected in a few weeks.
